event: Nala thinks fae silk may take a fae needle: the stem of one of the fallen leaves.
She picks the stiffest-stemmed birch leaf off the floor; it is still fresh and supple.
She snips the leaf away, pares the stem to a point and splits its end to hold thread.
At the silk's cut end the point slips in a hair's breadth; the weave doesn't draw back.
The stem folds soft in the middle, and a bead of green sap runs onto the silk.
Nala dabs it, and it spreads into a thumbnail-sized green stain that won't lift.
